newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's D'Alema talks with hard-left leader.
newsitem.headline: Italy's D'Alema talks with hard-left leader.

text.p: Massimo D'Alema, the leader of the Democratic Party of the Left, the biggest in Italy's coalition, met the head of Communist Refoundation on Thursday to discuss issues which risk jeopardising the government's stability.
A spokesman for the hard-left Communist Refoundation party said Fausto Bertinotti held 2-1/2 hours of talks with D'Alema.
"They tried to find positive solutions to the problems of the moment," he said.

Bertinotti, whose party holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament, has met leading government figures in recent days to try to resolve deep differences over a planned mini-budget, privatisations and a reform of the welfare state.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has pledged to introduce fresh a mini-budget in the coming weeks with up to 14.6 trillion lire ($8.5 billion) of deficit-cutting measures.

Bertinotti has already said he will not accept tax hikes or cuts to welfare spending, drastically limiting Prodi's options as he fights to contain the state deficit and book Italy a place on the launch of the single European currency.
The government and Refoundation are also negotiating over the planned sale later this year of telecom giant Stet, to which the hard-left is ideologically opposed.
The privatisation still needs parliamentary legislation and without a deal between Prodi and Bertinotti, the long delayed sell-off would be doomed to another postponment.

Corriere della Sera newspaper reported on Thursday that a meeting between Prodi and Bertinotti on Wednesday had been "icy". Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said the two sides were as far apart as ever.
